Article Title: For Kolkata’s football fans, Brazil was love before first sight
Article Text:
Graffiti in a Kolkata lane

As the city gears up to host Vini Jr & Co for tomorrow’s friendly, stars of India’s golden era talk of a lifelong romance ignited by match reports and the odd footage

Dreaming without visuals

Coach Datta’s Projector

From Argentine greats Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi to Germany’s Oliver Kahn, Kolkata has hosted some of football’s greatest icons down the years. Yet, the city holds a special place for Brazil, a love affair that began with its first breakout stars and is now set to only deepen when Vinicius Jr and his teammates arrive for the friendly they play against India on Saturday at Salt Lake Stadium.Coach Carlo Ancelotti’s boys are ranked No.6 in world football. India are a distant No.138. Some veterans have commented on the audacity of a lowly-ranked side taking on one of the giants of the game, but when Brazil first captured the imagination of football fans in India, it had more to do with a sense of kinship than purely adulation.Brazil’s rise coincided with India’s emergence as the superpower of Asian football, a golden era — notwithstanding the missed chance of taking part in the 1950 World Cup in Brazil — marked by triumphs at two Asian Games (1951, 1962) and a fourth-placed finish at the 1956 Olympics. As Brazil shook up football with its working-class, mixed-race team playing a unique brand of free-flowing football, India turned to it for inspiration.“During our time, we only wanted to play like Brazil. Because they were the No.1 team and we also wanted to be No.1,” former footballer Shyam Thapa told TOI. “We used to read a lot about Brazil in newspapers and were instantly drawn to this image of a team that might be economically poor like us but had the gift to conjure magic on the field and boss over European elites,” recalls Thapa.This was before the era of live telecast and highlight shows, with imagination filling in the details that reports could not convey. “Remember those were pre-TV days and we didn’t have the opportunity to watch Brazil live. So, we used to visualise their football magic in our own way. When Chuni-da dribbled past with one of his famous body feints, we would marvel at the move, saying it would make even Garrincha proud,” says Gautam Sarkar, a star footballer of the 1970s, referring to Indian legend Chuni Goswami and the Brazilian master considered to be among the greatest dribblers of the game.“In my mind, I discovered my Brazil through Kajol Mukherjee’s control and touch, Bengal Nagpur Railway star Rajendra Mohan’s running with and without the ball and, later, in Surajit Sengupta’s artistry,” adds Sarkar.But it wouldn’t be long before Kolkata found it could put faces to the names that set the city’s football pulse racing.Amal Datta’s career as a footballer never matched the ripples he would later create in his coaching avatar. Giving up his playing career prematurely to travel to England for a one-year FA coaching course, he returned in 1960 with a certificate that made him India’s first professional coach. In his luggage was a projector and grainy video clips that would give many in the city their first glimpse of Pele, Garrincha, Didi, Vava and Zagallo en route to winning the 1958 and 1962 World Cup finals.“Amal-da’s clippings on the projector screen became an absolute craze in the city during the 1960s. He also used to tell the audience to focus on and study the Brazilians’ movements on and off the ball,” recalls Sarkar.Then, in the 70s, came the documentary called, ‘Giants of Brazil’. “When it was screened for the first time at Lighthouse cinema, it resonated profoundly with the public,” says Gautam Roy, a football statistician. “Reading about Brazilian football and their artistes in newspapers and magazines was the sole source for firing our imagination. But seeing the documentary just drove up the craze,” he adds, noting how the hype would go on to hit stratospheric levels during Pele’s 1977 visit.Pele Comes CallingWhen Pele and his New York Cosmos club came calling, two of India’s top club sides presented a picture of contrasts. For Mohun Bagan, the club synonymous with awakenings of national pride, those were turbulent times. Their city rivals, East Bengal, had emerged as the undisputed rulers of Indian football and were still basking in the glow of their 5-0 thrashing of Bagan in the IFA Shield final of 1975.But, in 1976, Bagan general secretary Dhiren Dey pulled off a coup by snatching a host of players from East Bengal. It was around the same time that he learnt of Cosmos’s proposed tour of Asia. He quickly chalked out a plan to cash in on the visit. “I had already committed myself to East Bengal when he (Dey) proposed that I play for Bagan and grab the opportunity of taking the field against Pele. It was an offer too tempting for me to ignore,” says Shyam Thapa, who scored in the 2-2 tie against Cosmos at Eden Gardens on Sept 24, 1977.Saturday’s friendly comes at that time of the year when a sense of festivity drifts into Bengal’s air. As Kolkata gears up for Durga Puja, it will also look to embellish a deep bond that beats as part of its footballing heart. For both Sarkar and Thapa, the arrival of the Brazil team is like the journey coming full circle. Whatever the result, they know nothing can take away the bragging rights won nearly 50 years back: “the pride of playing against Pele”.
Article Summary: Kolkata has hosted some of football’s greatest icons down the years. The city holds a special place for Brazil, a love affair that began with its first breakout stars and is now set to only deepen when Vinicius Jr and his teammates arrive for the friendly.

Article Title: The midnight rescue of Karachi's Mahatma Gandhi
Article Text:
Gandhi statue outside the Sindh high court, Karachi (Picture credit: Haider Sherazi)

Gandhi statue in the Indian High Commission, Islamabad (Picture credit: Haider Sherazi)

G. Parthasarathy has served as India’s Consulate General in Karachi and as India’s High Commissioner in Islamabad.

One of the first things I did when I returned to Pakistan in early 2000, this time as the Indian High Commissioner, was to pay my respects to an imposing bronze statue of Mahatma Gandhi. One of only two Gandhi statutes in Pakistan, Bapuji stands tall at the lobby of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, famed walking stick in hand, gazing into the distance.The tale of how a pre-Partition statue found its way to its eventual home in the Indian High Commission is a fascinating saga reflecting the tangled tumultuous history of our two countries. It is a journey in which I was honoured to have played a small part.According to several accounts, the statue originally stood outside the Sindh high court on what was known as Kings Way in Karachi. It had been commissioned by the Indian merchant association sometime in the 1930s to commemorate the historic Karachi session of the Indian National Congress. The plaque underneath the life-size monument apparently read: “Mahatma Gandhi – the reputability of freedom, truth and nonviolence.Partition brought the inevitable dislocation. With communal riots engulfing Karachi in 1948, there was fear that the statue would be torn down amidst mob fury. Accounts vary on what exactly happened, but apparently after the intervention of Jamshed Nussranwanji Mehta, a Parsi and former Mayor of Karachi, the statue was surreptiously taken down and moved quietly to the home of the Cowasjees, a leading Parsi family of Karachi.And there it lay for more than thirty years…A few months into my first stint in Pakistan as Consul General in Karachi, a middle aged Parsi gentleman approached me. He was a well known Karachi businessman, activist and columnist whose name I am withholding. Over the course of several meetings he told me his incredible tale. How he as a young man along with several of his school chums insouciantly removed the Gandhi statue in the dead of the night armed with some basic tools and a lorry – all while Karachi seethed with fear and hatred. It was then ferried to his father’s home, initially meant as a temporary abode until a handover to Indian representative could be organised. Unfortunately, the then Indian High Commissioner to the Dominion of Pakistan could not assure a safe passage and refused. And that was how the Cowasjees became the involuntary guardians of Gandhi in PakistanThe Parsi gentleman was clear that his part in the story had to come to an end. We were now in the early 1980’s. General Zia’s Islamisation project was well underway. Sharia laws had been introduced into the legal system. Strict Islamic punishments were to be meted out for crimes like adultery, theft and drinking of alcohol. Educational curriculums were being rigorously overhauled to promote religious studies and conformity with orthodox Islamic principles. Dress codes, especially for women, were being enforced. The sari, once common amongst upper class Pakistani women, was fast disappearing. An ongoing media clampdown weeded out content deemed as un-Islamic.Though historically Parsis, unlike other minorities in Pakistan, have enjoyed a somewhat protected status and though Ardeshir was and continued to be a fearless and outspoken critic of the political establishment, he was no longer comfortable with his role as the statue’s custodian. He asked me if the long delayed handover of the statue could finally take place.I immediately agreed. I was determined that the statue, now a priceless historical artifact, should come home on my watch. There was, however, a tricky logistical issue to navigate. Constant surveillance by Pakistani intelligence was a fact of life. So how could we transport the statue without compromising the Cowasjees.After clearance from Delhi, we decided to replicate the original midnight run. A non-descript truck, organised by the Consulate, picked up a large wrapped item from the Cowasjee residence and quietly brought it to the Indian mission late one summer night.I personally inspected the precious cargo. Through all its travails, the statue had endured some damage. One hand was broken and the glasses were cracked, but otherwise Gandhiji stood tall. We arranged for some minor repairs, and after a few weeks, the statue took pride of place in the Chancery reception. Suddenly confronted with this majestic but serene statue, surprised Pakistani visitors were often curious about its origins, but we remained tightlipped.Eventually, once the statue was properly restored, we arranged for its transportation to the High Commission in Islamabad. In hindsight, that last trek from Karachi to Islamabad turned out to be as consequential as the original journey in 1948. In 1993, following the demolition of the Babri Masjid, furious mobs in Pakistan attacked over 30 Hindu temples and in Karachi ransacked both the Consulate and the Consul General’s residence in which I had once lived.Valuable art was vandalised, including a beautiful painting by B. Prabha.Post the 1993 attacks, the Indian consulate in Karachi closed down. It remains shut to this day. In Islamabad, however, the Gandhi statue still stands, an enduring testament to “freedom, truth and non-violence” true to its original plaque.
Article Summary: One of only two Gandhi statutes in Pakistan, Bapuji stands tall at the lobby of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad. The tale of how a pre-Partition statue found its way to its eventual home is a fascinating saga reflecting the tangled tumultuous history of our two countries.

Article Title: SP to field third candidate in UP Rajya Sabha polls? How move would trigger contest with BJP
Article Text:
The SP has so far announced two candidates, both of whom are assured of win

The arithemtic

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Virendra Singh on Friday announced that the party will field a third candidate in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, despite only two SP candidates being assured of victory.If the SP fields a third candidate, it would set up a contest with the ruling BJP for one seat. Seven BJP candidates are assured of victory. Polling for 10 vacant Rajya Sabha seats from the state is scheduled for October 16.“We will decide our third candidate today and the nomination will be filed by October 5,” Singh told PTI.The Chandauli MP further remarked that the SP would adopt the “same strategy” the BJP used to secure the election of its candidates in the previous Rajya Sabha polls.“We will get all three of our candidates elected through the same route by which the BJP had got its candidates elected in the last Rajya Sabha elections,” Singh added.He also claimed that several BJP MLAs seeking SP tickets for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections were in touch with the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.Singh’s remarks came a day after Akhilesh Yadav declined to confirm whether the SP would field a third candidate, suggesting that the BJP could put up “nine or even 10 candidates.”The SP on September 30 nominated veteran party leader and Akhilesh Yadav’s uncle, Ram Gopal Yadav, and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the elections. Both subsequently filed their nomination papers in Lucknow.The number of first-preference votes required to win a Rajya Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh depends on the number of vacancies and the number of MLAs eligible to vote. With 10 seats up for election this time, the winning benchmark is likely to be around 37 first-preference votes.The BJP currently has 255 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly, while its NDA allies have another 33, taking the alliance’s combined strength to 288.The SP has 101 MLAs. Three legislators who defected to the BJP are currently unattached, while rebel MLA Puja Pal remains listed with the SP despite having joined the BJP. The Congress, an SP ally, has two MLAs.In the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, the BJP won all eight seats it contested, while two of the SP’s three nominees were elected. The SP’s third candidate, Alok Ranjan, lost.Rajya Sabha elections are conducted through proportional representation using the single transferable vote system. Under this system, surplus votes received by winning candidates can be transferred to other candidates based on voters’ subsequent preferences.As a result, if more than 10 candidates enter the fray, the contest could hinge on the distribution and transfer of votes, making electoral arithmetic and strategy crucial.
Article Summary: The SP has so far announced two candidates, both of whom are assured of win. Polling for 10 vacant Rajya Sabha seats from the state is scheduled for October 16. If the SP fields a third candidate, it would set up a contest with the ruling BJP for one seat.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: Captain Smit Machchhar: A steady hand, in and out of the cockpit
Article Text:
Captain Smit Machchhar with his wife Sonal

.

Long before he was the captain who held a cockpit together despite stab wounds, Capt Smit Machchhar was the pilot who interacted with loaders, engineers, ground staff, catering people, all with equal respect.“Smit is the most calm, composed and down-to-earth person you could ever meet,” said Capt Dharav Gosalia, a friend since his flying school days.On Wednesday, that steadiness was tested at altitude. flydubai flight FZ1073 was carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv when, according to Israeli officials, Machchhar’s co-pilot stabbed him and tried to crash the aircraft. The jet reportedly dropped nearly 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Seriously wounded, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, letting passengers and crew overpower the attacker. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia.Those who know Machchhar, 39, are not surprised by how he behaved. What shocks them is that it was ever required. “He is one of the calmest and most fun guys possible,” said a friend, a B737 pilot who requested anonymity. “Maybe it is his upbringing. He is always in fun mode, but he is family-oriented too.”Machchhar earned his commercial pilot licence at Mainland Aviation College in New Zealand in the late 2000s, where he became the classmates’ go-to person for hard subjects. “Anyone with a problem in air navigation, aircraft technical or any subject went to him,” the pilot said. “Becoming a line trainer at flydubai was the best thing that could have happened to him.”The instinct to help was visible earlier, too. At M D Bhatia School, where he passed Class 10 in 2003, school friend Bhavin Jethva remembers him as “straightforward, bindass”. “He didn’t like to lie,” Jethva said. “He was never fake and he couldn’t pretend.” Amit Soni, a childhood friend who played cricket with him, called him cheerful and lively.At Swastik Heights in Mumbai’s Tilak Nagar, where Machchhar lived until about 2022, neighbour Laxmikanth Joshi remembers practical kindnesses. After returning from Kenya, Joshi realised he had bought too little coffee to share with friends. Machchhar arranged for a pilot colleague to bring back more. Joshi also remembers Machchhar going straight to the hospital after landing in India when his father underwent bypass surgery about six months ago. He stayed through the treatment. Then there were the Independence Day and Republic Day celebrations. He recalls Capt Machchhar taught them to tie the rope into a knot just right. “One pull and the flag unfurled,” recalled Joshi.Akshay Joshi, his immediate neighbour, recalls tense moments at his place when his parents learned about the attack. Late in the evening, though, Machchhar’s parents informed the society’s WhatsApp group that their son was recovering.Capt Machchhar moved to Dubai around 2022 after leaving SpiceJet, and flies the Boeing 737 as a captain and line trainer at flydubai. He and his wife, Sonal, have two children: Krishay, 2, and Ziva, 9.Friends and colleagues tried to reconstruct the sequence. A B737 commander said the co-pilot would most likely have used the ‘crash axe’, which is carried on the flight deck for use during emergencies, such as cutting through panels and debris, or the cockpit window to exit the aircraft after an accident. “At the Dubai airport, even shoes and belts are removed at security,” he said. “There’s no way the co-pilot could have got onboard with a pocket knife. ”Another colleague said the co-pilot “apparently stood up and hit Machchhar on the side of the head”. This colleague added that the captain was also struck in the chest, before he regained control after the dive. A third pilot said Machchhar appeared to have squawked ‘7500’, the hijack transponder code. A B737 commander also pointed to a gap: “We have SOPs for a hijack scenario, but not for a cockpit where the aggressor is inside.” He noted that Capt Machchhar’s bravery boils down to two acts: first, he managed to get the aircraft straight and level after that precarious dive, despite being attacked; second, though he had lost a lot of blood, he managed to open the cockpit door before he passed out.At M D Bhatia School, former classmates have been posting prayers for his recovery on their WhatsApp group. “We are proud of him,” Jethva said.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was the pilot who interacted with loaders, engineers, ground staff, catering people, all with equal respect. “Smit is the most calm, composed and down-to-earth person you could ever meet,” said a friend since his flying school days.

Article Title: Why Indian pilots struggle to take jobs abroad
Article Text:
A sand sculpture for Captain Smit Machchhar by artist Sudarshan Pattnaik in Puri, Odisha

NEW DELHI: At a time when pilots’ mental health has emerged as a key concern post some recent events, with flydubai cockpit fight being the most recent one, India’s restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress. The rule for a co-pilot to serve six months’ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally), has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire Indian aviators as they mostly want people to join in three months. Now with Captain Smit Machchhar proving his mettle in flydubai, the budget arm of Dubai’s mega carrier Emirates, Indian pilots hope foreign airlines — primarily in Gulf and other places like Sri Lanka and South Korea — keep the Indian reality in mind while giving them offer letters.“We usually don’t hire direct from India and prefer if a pilot has worked in a second country before onboarding them,” a senior official of a leading West Asian airline had recently told TOI. The reasons are two-fold: India’s notice period requirement, which remains binding for pilots even if the employer in India defaults on contractual obligations like paying on time, and then informal tie-ups with big Indian carriers against “poaching.A senior official of an airline here said: “Because of the notice period requirement, some pilots here give ‘fake resignation’ in advance and then look for jobs so that they can leave in three months of getting a job abroad. And if they don’t get a job, they take the fake resignation back.”The notice period rule has been challenged by pilots in court and the matter is sub judice. “There are concerns about pilots’ state of mind due to what could be going on in their personal lives. This notice period rule, meant to ensure schedule integrity of airlines by preventing sudden mass resignations, has outlived its utility. Today India has two big and well-funded airline and a few emerging ones. Now it is only protecting airlines that are unable to pay,” said a pilot.
Article Summary: India’s restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress. The rule for a co-pilot to serve six months’ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally) has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire Indian aviators.

Article Title: No uniform explanation for collegium decisions on compassionate transfers
Article Text:
The five-member collegium on Sept 28 recommended the repatriation of Justice T Vinod Kumar from Madras HC to his parent HC in Telangana 'in view of his ensuing retirement on Nov 16'

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court collegium's decisions to transfer judges from one HC to another are explained as being meant "for the better administration of justice". But the standard reasoning does not translate into a uniform explanation, with the collegium showing unusual compassion in approving requests from some for transfer or repatriation due to difficult family situations or health issues, while maintaining aloofness from others.There are many judges in HCs who have expressed resentment at the absence of any procedure or norm for transfer of HC judges. A member of the collegium, who will go on to become CJI, has mooted framing a transparent transfer policy. He told TOI that a judge under consideration for transfer should be warned first to mend his ways and be kept under watch for some time. Only when he does not improve should he be transferred, he said.The five-member collegium on Sept 28 recommended the repatriation of Justice T Vinod Kumar from Madras HC to his parent HC in Telangana "in view of his ensuing retirement on Nov 16". Justice Kumar was transferred from Telangana HC to Madras HC in May last year by the SC collegium headed by then CJI BR Gavai.In May last year, a complaint had reached the SC alleging that Justice Kumar, heading a division bench, had kept more than 50 judgments reserved.Sitting as a single judge, he had reserved verdicts in over 170 cases since 2020. If Justice Kumar's imminent retirement was a ground for his repatriation, no such consideration was shown to Justice D Nagarjun, who was transferred from Telangana HC to Madras HC. Justice Nagarjun, a career judicial officer who was elevated as an HC judge in March 2022, was transferred to Madras HC in April 2023.As he was due to retire on Aug 14, 2024, he sent a request to the CJI on July 25, 2024, for repatriation to his parent HC in Telangana, but the collegium remained aloof to the request and allowed him to retire in Madras HC.A Punjab and Haryana HC judge represented against his transfer to another HC, citing his wife's serious illness and disability of his child. But that evoked no compassion with the collegium, which remained firm on his transfer.Justice D V Ramana, who was only 13 years old when his railway gangman father died in an accident, rose from humble backgrounds to become a judge of Andhra Pradesh HC in Aug 2022. He was transferred to Madhya Pradesh HC in Nov 2023. On his retirement in May last year, he gave vent to his frustration. He said he was asked for options and chose Karnataka HC to enable better treatment for his wife, who had a neurological disorder. But that was not heeded. He again requested a transfer to Karnataka to help his wife get treated at Nimhans but that was neither considered nor rejected.
Article Summary: The five-member collegium on Sept 28 recommended the repatriation of Justice T Vinod Kumar from Madras HC to his parent HC in Telangana. If Justice Kumar's imminent retirement was a ground for his repatriation, no such consideration was shown to Justice D Nagarjun. A member of the collegium, who will go on to become CJI, has mooted framing a transparent transfer policy.

Article Title: 'INDIA Bloc stands united and will move forward collectively....it is not about individual decisions': Mamata

NEW DELHI: A day after the INDIA Alliance announced a joint agitation to demand the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise, Trinamool Congress Chairperson and former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee said that for the Opposition this was a “collective” fight and shared that she had promptly responded to CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby last week when he reached out to her over the working of the Election Commission as it was a "national issue".Reports of the interaction between Baby and Banerjee had attracted much attention last week as it saw two parties with decades-long differences in Bengal coming together on the question of the Election Commission (EC).Banerjee shared details of the interaction and the sentiment behind both sides putting aside their differences and coming together, while responding to questions at a press conference in Delhi. Party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and senior party leaders Derek O' Brien, Dola Sen, Mahua Moitra, Menaka Guruswamy and Saket Gokhale were among those present with Mamata Banerjee at the press conference.“Our position is that when Constitutional institutions and democratic rights are at stake, political parties should examine the issue beyond their individual colours and interests,” Banerjee asserted.When asked about Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the question of leadership of the opposition alliance and her view on who can be the Bloc's PM candidate, the TMC Chairperson said, "INDIA Alliance is United and together. It is not about individual decisions. We are like a family, and we will decide collectively on these issues.""Regional political parties have their own circumstances and compulsions, and we understand that. We maintain good relations with leaders such as Arvind Kejriwal (AAP), Nitish Kumar (JDU) and MK Stalin (DMK), while local political decisions may differ from state to state. Sometimes, INDIA's alliance partners may not attend a particular programme because of local political considerations, but that does not necessarily mean there is disagreement on broader national issues,” she added.“We are with the INDIA alliance, and whatever decisions the alliance takes, we will respect them like a family and work together with unity. Our priority is to stand together and move forward collectively,” Banerjee said.“2029 is still far away; first, look at what is happening in 2027. “Khela toh ab hoga” — the real political game begins now. You never know what may happen in the next two, three, or six months. Politics can change very quickly, and we will continue to watch the situation, remain united and make decisions together as an alliance,” she emphasised.“It is important for Gyanesh Kumar to go...change is critical at this stage to make way for a free and fair electoral system,” Banerjee said in response to a question about whether the resignation of CEC would help resolve the systemic problems.TMC national general secretary and Lok Sabha MP Abhishek Banerjee lashed out, saying, "When questions are directed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar or the Election Commission, I believe the answers should come from the Election Commission itself. Instead, we repeatedly see BJP leaders responding to those questions. My point is simple: constitutional authorities must answer legitimate questions themselves and place facts before the public rather than allowing political parties to speak on their behalf. " He called for a thorough investigation to bring out the truth.

Article Title: Amrinder Singh Raja Warring changes X bio after stepping down as Punjab Congress chief
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state amid a factional feud.This comes hours after Warring declined to comment on reports that the party high command had decided to replace him, saying that “some issues are internal”.The move comes after months of infighting within the Punjab Congress, which intensified after the party high command decided on July 1 to retain Warring as the state unit chief.A section of leaders led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had opposed Warring’s continuation and sought his removal. Leaders aligned with the Channi camp also stayed away from party programmes led by Warring.According to PTI, the Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge held a series of meetings with state leaders before submitting his report to the party high command on the proposed leadership change.The high command subsequently informed Warring of its decision, party sources told PTI, adding that the Congress is now looking to appoint a leader who can bring different factions together ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Former minister and ex-MP Vijay Inder Singla has emerged as a frontrunner for the post, sources said. The other names being discussed include former Olympian and Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa.The leadership tussle has played out publicly in recent months, raising concerns within the party over its impact on the Congress campaign as it seeks to return to power in Punjab.The factionalism has also added to concerns over the party’s ability to consolidate its organisation ahead of the assembly polls.Asked about the possibility of a change in the Punjab Congress leadership on Tuesday, Channi said the decision was the prerogative of the party high command.“It is the prerogative of Rahul Gandhi and (Mallikarjun) Kharge ji. Only they know who is to be appointed or when is to be changed,” Channi told reporters in Delhi.Warring had also faced criticism from sections of the party over the Congress’ electoral performance in Punjab and his leadership.In August, he defended himself against criticism over the party’s decline in the 2022 assembly elections, questioning attempts to hold him responsible for the loss.“The only mistake is that when the Congress Party had 80 seats, we came down from 80 to 18 seats. Is that my fault? Captain Amarinder Singh led the government twice. From 80 seats, we came down to 18 seats,” he had said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" This comes amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state. Vijay Inder Singla, Pargat Singh, Rana KP Singh and Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria are among those being considered.

Article Title: Aaron Rodgers says there is "zero debate" about retiring, yet his final Thursday night game feels like unfinished business
Article Text:

Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m. ET on Amazon Prime. He sits one win short of tying Tom Brady's record of 14 Thursday wins by a quarterback. Both teams are 2-1. The Steelers beat Cincinnati 30-27 last week, and the Browns edged Carolina 21-18. Pittsburgh also arrives with an 0-9 mark in Thursday road games against AFC North opponents. Rodgers, 42, plans to retire after this 22nd season, so Cleveland is his final shot at matching Brady's number.Everything he has said points to yes. Rodgers signed a one-year deal with Pittsburgh in May after more than four months of deliberating. Asked whether this would be his last season, he told reporters, “Yes, this is it.” When he returned to training camp on July 28, a reporter asked if he was weighing another year after this one. His answer was short. “No. Zero debate.”That certainty changes how Thursday reads. Rodgers turns 43 in December, and this is his last scheduled Thursday game. Brady's mark is 14, so a win ties it and nothing more. There is no later date to push past him.Rodgers has 46 touchdowns and seven interceptions on Thursdays. Against Cleveland, he has thrown 11 touchdowns without an interception in five games.He does not sound sentimental about the night itself. “I just suck it up for those three hours and then know you get a reward on the back end. I think it’s part of the game now because of the money that’s in it. I think I’m just excited about the weekend,” Rodgers said. If the Brady record matters to him, he is keeping it quiet.History says be careful. Pittsburgh has lost all nine Thursday road games against AFC North teams, and four of those came against Cleveland. The Browns won 24-19 in a snowstorm two years ago. The 2019 meeting is remembered for Myles Garrett ripping off Mason Rudolph's helmet and hitting him with it. Cleveland has also won seven straight Thursday games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in NFL history.Defensive tackle Cam Heyward does not see the short week as a one-sided problem. “But the great thing about it is they got to deal with the same problems we are. So it’s an even playing field,” he said.The Steelers have roster questions, though. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. went to Dallas late Wednesday for two draft picks after a contract impasse, and Jalen Ramsey is questionable with a broken wrist. Jaylen Warren should carry the load again after a career-high 176 total yards against Cincinnati, since Rico Dowdle is out with a toe injury.The line play may decide it. Browns tackles have allowed a 13.5% pressure rate, second highest in the league, and Tytus Howard's 17 pressures are tied for the most by a right tackle. TJ Watt has 17.5 sacks in 15 games against Cleveland. Deshaun Watson has lost all three starts against Pittsburgh and been sacked 18 times. Mike McCarthy is 11-5 on Thursday nights, and the Steelers are 2.5-point favorites.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark’s latest WNBA punishment explained: Fever guard’s Brianna Turner clash adds drama to Game 3 showdown vs Aces
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark was hit with a technical foul. Image via: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Caitlin Clark receives technical foul after shoving Brianna Turner

How close is Caitlin Clark to a WNBA playoff suspension?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark picked up a technical foul in the opening minutes of a win-or-go-home Game 3, and the cause was a former teammate who showed up inside Indiana's huddle. Brianna Turner got one too. Nobody shot a free throw, but the call put her playoff run on thinner ice.It happened Thursday, Oct. 1, in Las Vegas, with 6:54 left in the first quarter and officials still reviewing a foul on A'ja Wilson. The Fever were up 12-6. Then came the shove, a theatrical stumble and a double whistle.Caitlin Clark's technical in Game 3 against the Las Vegas Aces grew out of a play that began with someone else. Fever forward Lexie Hull was whistled for fouling Wilson on a rebound attempt. Referees went to the monitor to decide whether the call should be upgraded.While they checked, Indiana's starters gathered on the floor. Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, Hull, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson formed a quick huddle. Brianna Turner was standing nearby, and she drifted into the circle. The Fever guard did not appear to say a word. She walked straight up to Turner and pushed her out.Turner flung her arms up and staggered back, selling the contact for all it was worth.Turner played for Indiana in 2025, so the two know each other well. Whether Turner was hunting for information or just trying to break the group's focus is hard to say, though it looked like one or the other.After the review, officials gave both players a technical. Because the calls offset, neither team went to the line.The Fever guard had been here before. Her first technical of the postseason came Tuesday in Game 2, when Clark was called for an offensive foul after pushing Las Vegas guard Mai Yamamoto and appeared to wave off the official. It is unclear whether Clark said anything that earned the technical. Indiana trailed 29-20 at that point and then ripped off a 28-14 run.Closer than the Fever would like. Under WNBA rules, a player or coach is suspended for one game when the fourth technical of the postseason is called. Clark has two, so the Indiana guard sits halfway there. Each technical after that costs $1,500, and every two more adds another one-game ban.Counts reset when the regular season ends. Clark finished with seven, one short of the eighth that would have forced a suspension, so the playoffs began with a clean slate. The league can also review and rescind technicals, which means no total is final until the WNBA says so.Game 3 carried its own risk. With a technical already on the books, a second one in the same game would have meant an ejection for either player.The series had already been intense. Las Vegas won Game 1 at home, and Indiana forced this decider with a win at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday. Wilson drew a controversial conduct technical in that game after confronting a fan under the baseline.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark was given a technical foul for shoving Brianna Turner. The incident happened in the first quarter of Game 3 of the Indiana Fever's playoff series with the Las Vegas Aces. A technical in the same game would have meant an ejection for either player.

Article Title: How DK Metcalf turned NFL stardom into a $30 million net worth with a $132 million Steelers contract and lucrative endorsements
Article Text:
DK Metcalf's Net Worth (Imagn Images)

How did DK Metcalf build a $30 million net worth?

What is in DK Metcalf's $132 million Steelers contract?

Does DK Metcalf earn money from endorsements?

DK Metcalf's net worth sits at an estimated $30 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. That figure looks small next to the four-year, $132 million extension he signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers in March 2025 after a trade from Seattle. The deal includes a $30 million signing bonus and $60 million guaranteed at signing. Add endorsements with Gatorade, Nesquik and eBay, and the gap between contract value and net worth starts to make sense. Much of the Steelers money is still to be paid, and the estimate may lag behind it.Metcalf's money story started modestly. As the 64th pick in 2019, he signed a rookie deal worth about $4.6 million with a $1.4 million signing bonus. That was modest for a player who would break Seattle's single-season receiving record in 2020 with 1,303 yards.The first real jump came in July 2022. Seattle gave him a three-year, $72 million extension with $58.2 million guaranteed and a $30 million signing bonus. At $24 million a year, that deal is likely where most of his wealth was built, and it matches the $24 million salary Celebrity Net Worth lists.Still, net worth is not salary added up. Taxes, agent fees and living costs take a big share of every NFL paycheck.That helps explain why a player with years of eight-figure pay is pegged at $30 million.Pittsburgh acquired Metcalf from Seattle for a second-round pick and signed him to a four-year, $132 million extension, the biggest contract in franchise history. It averages $33 million a year. The $30 million signing bonus and $60 million guaranteed at signing matter most for his bank balance, because that money is locked in.The deal has already been tested. Metcalf received a two-game suspension in December 2025 after striking a Detroit Lions fan. It could have voided about $45 million in future guarantees, but Jay Glazer reported the Steelers chose not to. Before the 2026 season, Pittsburgh also restructured the contract, turning part of his base salary into a signing bonus. That freed nearly $18 million in cap space and did not cut his pay.That timing matters for the $30 million figure. The Celebrity Net Worth page shows a March 2025 update date, so it may not fully count the Steelers signing bonus and the Pittsburgh paychecks that followed.Yes, though endorsements likely make up a smaller piece of the picture. Celebrity Net Worth lists Gatorade, Nesquik and eBay among his brand partners. Exact fees are not public, so any figure on that side is a guess.What is clear is why brands like him. The colored mouthpieces, the visor and the occasional blue hair make him easy to spot, and his 4.33-second 40-yard dash at the 2019 combine still gets shared online.His profile also got a lift off the field. He announced his engagement to singer Normani in March 2025, which put his name in entertainment headlines as well as sports ones.Production still drives that value, though. Metcalf did not reach 1,000 yards in his first Pittsburgh season, yet he stayed one of Aaron Rodgers' most reliable targets and helped the Steelers make the playoffs. A bigger 2026 would give sponsors more to work with.
Article Summary: DK Metcalf's net worth sits at an estimated $30 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. That figure looks small next to the four-year, $132 million extension he signed with the Steelers. Add endorsements with Gatorade, Nesquik and eBay, and the gap starts to make sense.

Article Title: Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James? Spurs star drops candid reaction after NBA veteran’s eyebrow-raising Polymarket deal
Article Text:

Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James?

How other NBA stars have taken betting money

Victor Wembanyama has recently gave his honest reaction to the sports betting debate. At Spurs training camp on Thursday, a reporter asked whether the San Antonio center would ever promote a gambling company. "Absolutely not," he replied instantly. He further explained why he is dead set on staying out of it.The reigning Defensive Player of the Year spoke just weeks after LeBron James signed a Polymarket partnership expected to pay him $15 million a year. Wembanyama never mentioned the 76ers star by name but he certainly appears to take aim at the NBA veteran.Victor Wembanyama was answering a general question about sports betting sponsorships, and he spoke about the practice rather than one player. Asked on Thursday, October 1, he called it "very sad to see some players promote it." Then he added a line with a little edge, everybody does what they want, but without him.For those who have been aware of LeBron James's Polymarket deal, it certainly looks like an apparent slam at James, and the 76ers star is the obvious reference point. The 41-year-old announced a multi-year Polymarket partnership a few weeks ago, and he is expected to earn $15 million a year from it.James also signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Philadelphia this summer. One year of Polymarket money is worth more than that entire deal.Wembanyama explained the reasoning without pointing at anyone. "Obviously, we earn millions and millions," he said, before moving the conversation to influence. A player's biggest strength, according to the Spurs big man, is the ability to inspire, and that can go in a good direction or a bad one. "I want to inspire in a good way."Wembanyama has turned down endorsement offers before when the values behind them did not match. He does sign deals, though. A new Nike agreement includes a signature sneaker line.Wembanyama is stepping away from a crowded field. Giannis Antetokounmpo took an equity stake in Kalshi in February, and the Miami Heat star handles promotional work for the prediction market too. Kevin Durant has turned up regularly in FanDuel commercials, and his entertainment network, Boardroom, is partnered with the company. James had a similar arrangement with DraftKings before the Polymarket deal.Betting sponsorships have gone mainstream as the major leagues embrace gambling, and several NBA names now work with betting companies or prediction markets. More current and retired athletes could follow as the industry keeps growing. Wembanyama has said he will never be one of them.
Article Summary: Victor Wembanyama said he would never promote a sports betting company. The San Antonio Spurs center made the comments at Spurs training camp. LeBron James recently announced a multi-year Polymarket partnership. James is expected to earn $15 million a year from the deal.

Article Title: 20 golds lost, just one individual title won: India’s Asian Games slide offers a stark reality check
Article Text:
Manu Bhaker and Satwik-Chirag (Agency Image)

A different gold-medal profile

Two more chances

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With the Asian Games entering the final stretch, India’s declining gold medal numbers tell an uncomfortable story and offer a sharp reality check. Of the 28 golds India won in Hangzhou three years ago, 20 have already slipped away in Aichi-Nagoya, across shooting, athletics, archery, badminton, equestrian, squash and tennis. The sharpest contrast comes in individual events. In Hangzhou, India won nine individual gold medals across shooting, athletics and archery. None of those have been defended and, in some events, India was not even able to make the final rounds in the ongoing edition.In 2023, India produced a historic 106-medal haul: 28 gold, 38 silver and 40 bronze. Shooting alone delivered seven golds and athletics six, while archery completed a clean sweep of all five compound golds.Three years later, India has lost all seven shooting golds it won in Hangzhou and all six in athletics. In archery, the three team titles have survived, but neither of the individual ones. In squash, the country has lost both its titles from 2023 in the men’s team event and mixed doubles. The Hangzhou golds in badminton men’s doubles, team dressage and tennis mixed doubles have also not been retained.As of Thursday, India has won 10 gold medals at Aichi-Nagoya, with men’s hockey and cricket still carrying title-defence possibilities.India’s overall medal tally has crossed 60 and the country is eighth overall, but it is staring at a far lower haul than at Hangzhou. For perspective, China has so far won 154 gold medals and 288 medals overall.Particularly worrying is the disappearance of gold medals that India had already established as its continental benchmark.India’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya has produced its share of memorable performances, new champions and hard-earned podium finishes. But with just two days left for the continental event to wind up, the larger picture is difficult to ignore: India has not been able to build on the gold-medal gains of Hangzhou.The six successful defences have come in men’s and women’s kabaddi, all three compound archery team events and women’s cricket. In Aichi-Nagoya, among the 10 gold medals won by India so far, only one has come in an individual event: Neeru Dhanda’s historic women’s trap triumph.The rest have come through team, relay or mixed formats. That is a substantial shift in the profile of India’s gold-medal success.India is not finished. The men’s hockey team has reached the gold-medal match after narrowly beating Pakistan 4-3 in the semifinal. The men’s cricket team has also reached the final, where it will face Pakistan after beating Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semifinal.If India wins these two, the Hangzhou-to-Aichi-Nagoya comparison will improve from six successful defences to eight. But even a two-from-two finish would leave the basic statistic untouched: 20 of the Hangzhou golds would still have been lost.That is the number that should concern Indian sport administrators.It is not merely a case of one or two champions falling short. It points to a much broader problem of converting a successful Asian Games cycle into sustained dominance.The athletes who have won medals in Japan deserve full credit. The question is different: what happened between a record 28-gold campaign in Hangzhou and a Games in which the majority of those titles have not been retained?The answer cannot be found merely in the final medal table.Hangzhou demonstrated that India could win 28 golds. Aichi-Nagoya is demonstrating how difficult it is to make those gains sustainable.From 28 golds to 10: India’s Asian Games slide offers a stark reality check
Article Summary: Of the 28 golds India won in Hangzhou three years ago, 20 have already slipped away in Aichi-Nagoya, across shooting, athletics, archery, badminton, equestrian, squash and tennis. The sharpest contrast comes in individual events. In Hangzhou, India won nine individual gold medals. None of those have been defended and, in some events, India was not even able to make the final rounds.

Article Title: Iowa teacher asked students to donate to her GoFundMe to fund her medical mission trip to Ecuador, promised extra credit
Article Text:
Iowa teacher promised extra credits to students if they donate to her GoFundMe to fund her travel to Ecuador.

An Iowa substitute teacher has been fired from her post for allegedly pressuring her students to help fund her "medical mission" to Ecuador. Stephanie Mullaley promised them extra credit for donating to her GoFundMe page. Iowa Capital Dispatch reported that the trip was planned in July but her action came to notice that and she was removed in May.“(She) promised high school students in her class that they would receive extra credit toward their grade in her class if they donated to her GoFundMe account. Students felt pressured to donate money to her personal GoFundMe page,” Administrative Law Judge Duane Golden said.Despite such arm-twisting, Mullaley could gather only $140 as against her target of $1800. The fundraiser was deleted.“Nick & I are embarking on a journey this summer with a medical mission group,” Mullaley wrote on a Facebook post alongside the link to the defunct fundraiser. “This was only a thought a year ago, and it became real when we got an official invitation end of 2025.“Feels like a blessing to have an opportunity to serve a community in need of medical service and utilize my skills and serve. God put this in place for us, and we’re answering it,” she wrote.“Hope to have your support, and if you can’t financially, we understand and just keep us in your prayers.”Mullaley pleaded with her students that the experience would “pay for her education” because it was a “unique opportunity to travel to Ecuador” where she would be interpreting the mission trip. “Helping bridge language barriers so that care and compassion can reach those who need it most,” and that her husband would be “assisting the team in any way he can,” Mullaley wrote.The judge denied ex-teacher unemployment benefits and said the teacher demonstrated a "willful or wanton disregard" of her employer's interests.
Article Summary: Stephanie Mullaley promised her students extra credit if they donated to her GoFundMe page. Mullaley could gather only $140 as against her target of $1800. The judge denied ex-teacher unemployment benefits and said the teacher demonstrated a "willful or wanton disregard" of her employer's interests.

Article Title: ‘If India won a medal, we owe it to her’: Captain Swayams Mishra on Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad heroics | Exclusive
Article Text:

The coffee, the bananas, and the helplessness of watching

Build-up: Virtual camps, and logistics that nearly derailed things again

The Vaishali decision

Board-by-board analysis from the captain

Bronze, and what the team takes from it

NEW DELHI: Across the open and women's sections at the Chess Olympiad, only one player won an individual gold medal for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. That was Chennai's 19-year-old Savitha Shri Baskar. Savitha was often the one India could rely on when the team was staring at heartbreak. With her games routinely going down to the wire, she was kept fuelled, game after game, by someone making sure she never had to think about anything other than the board during India's bronze-clinching campaign."If we wanted something, he was always there, giving us everything, like water, bananas, and for me, he was bringing endless coffees because I played till the last moment, making sure that I ate properly and got energy," Savitha recalled, before labelling Swayams Mishra as the "best captain ever".For Mishra, it was new territory in a role he'd long been adjacent to."I've been part of the women's team since 2022, but this was the first time I was captaining completely. In 2024, I had captained for a couple of games, but this was a completely new experience," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction."This time, I have to be there in the tournament hall with the players, especially in the critical games, so the emotions are completely different compared to when you are outside.That was slightly different, and not easy."The job, according to Mishra, was less about tactics and more about manoeuvres of a different kind."It was hectic and exhausting, because as a captain you try to follow all the games going on, not just one player's. At the same time, sometimes you see a player making a mistake; you want to do something, but you cannot; you just have to wait for it to unfold naturally," he admitted. What he could control, though, he controlled."What I tried to do is look at what the players needed. If there's a longer game, they needed some energy or something to eat, so I made sure they had it available instead of spending time getting it themselves around the third or fourth hour."Viewers watching the live broadcast of the games got to witness the results of that instinct in real time, with water bottles, bananas, and coffee cups appearing at just the right moments.The challenges for Swayams started even before the tournament. Getting the team to that stage was a project in itself, with busy, overlapping schedules making it difficult for the players to train together in person.With the help of the All India Chess Federation (AICF), the team turned to virtual camps in the run-up to the Olympiad."It all started with the camps, like organising the camp online, where we found that most of the players' schedules were very tight, so we held an online camp because players were not able to find a common timing to able to meet up with their busy schedules," Mishra revealed.The challenges followed the team in Samarkand, where India, like several other nations, faced accommodation and food issues."On the first day, with the issues with the stay, AICF stepped up, and the president Nitin Narang and the HOD Abhijit Kunte ensured that the players got the rooms first," he said. "President Narang was also present, and he went out of his way to help us in most of the things."Food then became another issue, with Mishra recalling that “when food was not very ideal, the options were not great, AICF made sure that food is Indian food people get so that they don't lack energy and they don't go like let's say their routine and other things are not disturbed as well.”The team bronze did not come easy, without its share of difficult calls. One of the toughest was deciding which four players from the five-member squad would take the board each round."For me, it was not easy choosing whom to play, because it was always a tricky call, with Savitha and Vantika performing very well on the last boards, and Vaishali also having good chances; we wanted her to play. It's a very hard call when one of your top players ends up not being in form, and the others are performing very well. Vaishali tried, gave her best, but it just wasn't meant to be," the captain, who then decided to keep the Women's World Championship challenger on the board for only six out of the eleven games, sighed.With Vaishali, who had just one win in the entire Olympiad and finished with a score of 2.5/6, due to challenge for the Women's World Championship title next year, Mishra also addressed whether this stretch of poor form carried any psychological weight into that bigger picture."We had a discussion, and she was not thinking at all about the World Championship. She wanted to just focus and give her best for India in this Olympiad, but it wasn't working out. I think she's strong enough, a professional player who should be able to get back much stronger and prove herself as a world champion as well. I wish she wins the World Championship.""Humpy on board one, I think, this would be her best Olympiad. India hadn't won a medal on board one for quite some time, and her winning one (a bronze with a score of 7/10), undefeated, against strong opposition, was very good. We were never on the back foot on board one," captain Mishra explained.Board two, however, told a different story."Vaishali started off decently. She had some tough opponents who didn't make mistakes and played precisely against her. Against Poland, that's where things changed — she had a better position, in fact, and wanted to win. There were a couple of chances to simplify into a draw, but she wanted to win, and in that process ended up making mistakes and losing," the coach added."Then she had another critical game against Kazakhstan, where she again had chances to equalise but wanted to win it for the team. A draw there would have given us 2-2, because Savitha's board wasn't clear yet. So she tried, and it backfired. You can say she was always there for the team, even if her performance wasn't great."By contrast, individual silver medalist Divya Deshmukh, scoring 6.5/10, emerged as one of the pillars."She took a lot of blacks, seven out of ten games, and was always ready whenever the team needed her. She had a consistent performance and gave us a couple of fast wins that put pressure on the other opponents."It came after a rough patch as Mishra continued, "She started completely out of form; Cairns Cup wasn't as per expectations, GCL wasn't great. But from there, she came back very strongly and was always reliable. She lost the last round, but she'd done her job by then."Vantika Agrawal, on board four for most of the tournament before Savitha's emergence, drew measured praise."She was consistent. There was one game, against China, that was very close, where she was close to a draw and missed something under pressure. Otherwise, she did her job, whatever was assigned to her, and gave us points on the last board," he added.And then Savitha. Mishra didn't hold back on addressing the scrutiny that had followed her selection."There were a lot of people who questioned her spot, journalists saying there are players higher than her, and so on. But according to the selection, she was qualified, and she'd won the Asian continental a couple of months ago. She'd also played the World Women's Team Championship, so I knew her as a team player always."Whenever we gave her the opportunity, she delivered. From round seven onwards, her form dropped slightly compared to the initial rounds as she was making some errors; the quality wasn't quite what she'd have expected. But she always compensated in the last hour, changing the result of the match completely. If India won a medal, we owe it to her."Asked whether anyone inside the camp was satisfied with bronze, Mishra didn't pretend otherwise."We are not satisfied. The colour of the medal would have been different, and we would have been much happier. But even in your not-so-good times, if you're able to get a medal, that shows how strong the team is. We expect to come back even stronger next year and win gold."I know people might be disappointed; the fans might be disappointed; we're equally disappointed. But everyone tried their best. The margins were very close."The tournament's bigger lesson, for him, had less to do with India specifically than with the state of women's chess as a whole."We did not underestimate anyone, but there were a lot of teams creating upsets. Mongolia, whom we played in round four, and Greece in round three, both ended up causing upsets elsewhere. Against the silver-winning Kazakh team, Mongolia were winning too, before it finished 2-2. In the last few Olympiads it was smooth sailing for the top seeds.This year, weaker teams were able to strike. That means chess is growing in general, especially women's chess. "ALSO READ: 'Unrealistic to win gold every single time': Captain Srinath Narayanan after India's silver at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive It's a tournament Mishra will remember as much for its margins as its medal, a campaign where India were, by his own description, "always on the wrong side of where we wanted to be", rescued more than once by a teenager fuelled on endless cups of coffee, and still, somehow, bronze rather than nothing at all.
Article Summary: India won bronze at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Captain Swayams Mishra described the experience as hectic and exhausting. Savitha Shri Baskar was often the one India could rely on when the team was facing heartbreak.
