Article Title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
Article Text:
She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. Her years of borrowed independence came to an end as she was sent back to jail.
Article Summary: Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005. Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar. The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda holds her nerve to clinch Asian Games boxing gold in 3-2 thriller
Article Text:
India's Parveen Hooda (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lovlina ends India's 12-year wait

Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women's 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games , beating Chinese Taipei's Chen Nien-Chen 3-2 in a split decision in a closely fought final.The Indian boxer had to dig deep in the deciding round after Chen levelled the contest following two rounds. Parveen held her nerve in a tense finish, relying on her counter-punching as the Chinese Taipei boxer pressed for the decisive blows.The victory adds another boxing gold for India on a day when Lovlina Borgohain also stood atop the podium.Parveen made a cautious start to the final, with both boxers initially keeping their distance. She found success with her counters before stepping in with combinations, including some effective body shots. The judges awarded her the opening round 5-0.Chen responded in the second round. Parveen continued to use her reach and movement to keep her opponent at bay, but Chen found her range with quick 1-2 combinations and landed enough clean punches to take the round 10-9 on all five cards.With the scores level heading into the final round, Chen came out aggressively and landed a couple of early jabs.Parveen weathered the pressure and began finding openings with quick combinations of her own.The Indian then switched to counter-punching as Chen pushed forward in the closing stages. The strategy proved enough to edge the contest, with Parveen winning the final by a 3-2 split decision.The gold marks a significant turnaround for Parveen, whose medal from the Hangzhou Asian Games was revoked following a doping violation. She had also exited the 2026 Commonwealth Games at the quarterfinal stage.Chen, a former world champion, came into the final as the 2026 Asian Championships gold medallist and had also won bronze at the previous Asian Games and the Paris Olympics.Earlier on Friday, Lovlina Borgohain ended India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final.The Olympic bronze medallist secured a 5-0 unanimous decision to upgrade the silver medal she won at the previous edition, giving herself a gold medal on her birthday.Lovlina became only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold. Mary Kom had claimed the 51kg title at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain ends India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final. Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women’s 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games.

Article Title: In 2021, a former RAF site in Oxfordshire became 187 homes, with 160 made from old barracks, mess halls and stores once built for military life
Article Text:
Apartments in the Garden Quarter at Caversfield, Oxfordshire, where former RAF buildings were converted into homes | Wikimedia Commons

Apartments in the Garden Quarter at Caversfield, Oxfordshire, where former RAF buildings were converted into homes | Wikimedia Commons

160 old buildings became homes

New houses were fitted around the old ones

Existing structures were converted, while new homes were inserted where they could fit the historic layout | Wikimedia Commons

From military quarters to a residential community

A former Royal Air Force site in Caversfield, Oxfordshire, now contains 187 homes, with 160 of them sitting inside buildings that were originally designed for military life. Barracks and mess buildings at the former RAF Bicester domestic site were converted into homes, while 27 new houses were added around them.The residential development was known as the Garden Quarter, and occupies what was once the domestic side of RAF Bicester. It was separate from the technical site and airfield across the road and was built to accommodate the people who worked at the base. RAF Bicester is recognised as one of the most intact early 20th-century military sites in England by Historic England . The Caversfield domestic area retained groups of buildings that were associated with everyday military life, including barracks, mess buildings and stores. Twelve individual buildings on the site have Grade II listed status. Caversfield Parish Council notes that RAF Bicester is no longer operational and that the former domestic site on Skimmingdish Lane has been redeveloped as the Garden Quarter. The airfield and the historic buildings that surround it are now associated with Bicester Motion, while the former residential and support area has taken on a new use.The unusual part of the project was the decision to keep the military buildings and work within their existing arrangement. The original planning application that was approved in 2011 called for the conversion of buildings into 160 dwellings, alongside the construction of 27 new dwellings. It also included plans to turn one lodge building into a shop and café, with another building retaining a storage use.The conversion meant that buildings that were once associated with RAF accommodation and communal life could remain part of the site's physical layout. Historic England says that modern additions had accumulated on the site and were demolished to reveal the historic buildings more clearly. New houses were then positioned in relation to the surviving structures rather than ignoring them. The military planners had originally laid out the domestic area with generous spaces between buildings, and Historic England notes that the spacing had been designed partly to reduce the potential impact of bomb damage. The redevelopment retained those relationships instead of filling the site with tightly packed new construction.Architects Feilden+Mawson positioned the new houses to align with the existing military buildings, and at the northern end of the site, two new residential terraces were placed around the open space in front of the former Officers' Mess and the former Dining Room and Institute. Large areas of hard surfacing and parking had previously dominated parts of the site, but those areas were reduced and three landscaped garden squares were introduced, which created open spaces between the residential buildings.Some of the restoration work was small but visible, and Historic England notes that mismatched windows and chimney pots were replaced, while sections of pointing that did not match the original brickwork were removed and repaired. The intention was to make the buildings read as a coherent group again.Historic England says that there were concerns about domestic use, which could conflict with the distinctive military character of the buildings. The redevelopment therefore had to balance two competing demands of preserving a site that had a strong military identity while making the buildings practical for modern housing.Existing structures were converted, while new homes were inserted where they could fit the historic layout, and the result was a development of 187 residential units rather than a wholesale replacement of the former RAF buildings. Historic England's current heritage-housing database lists the Garden Quarter as 160 homes in historic buildings and 27 in the new-build element, with the project recorded as completed in 2024. The buildings that once supported RAF personnel now have a different daily rhythm, with former barracks becoming residential blocks, spaces that were once used for communal military life having new occupants, and the parade-ground setting having been reshaped into landscaped residential space.
Article Summary: RAF Bicester is recognised as one of the most intact early 20th-century military sites in England by Historic England. Barracks and mess buildings at the former RAF Bicester domestic site were converted into homes, while 27 new houses were added around them.

Article Title: Terence Crawford opens up on why his resume is “night and day” better than UFC legend Khabib Nurmagomedov
Article Text:
Terence Crawford (via Getty Images)

Terence Crawford explains why he rates his resume above Khabib Nurmagomedov’s

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Terence Crawford has made a bold claim about his boxing legacy. The undefeated former champion believes his resume is far more impressive than Khabib Nurmagomedov’s MMA record. Crawford said the difference between their careers is “night and day” while pointing to the quality and variety of opponents he has faced.Crawford also highlighted his decision to move up two weight divisions to fight Canelo Álvarez. The American boxer believes taking on elite opponents across several weight classes gives his career an edge. Crawford retired undefeated after becoming an undisputed champion in multiple divisions.Terence Crawford has never been short of confidence when discussing his place among boxing’s greats. His latest comments put his career resume directly against that of former UFC lightweight champion Khabib Nurmagomedov.The American believes his achievements in boxing stand above Khabib’s accomplishments in MMA.“I’ve fought everybody there is to fight. Moving up two divisions to fight Canelo? My record is more impressive, for sure”, he said via Complex Sports.Crawford’s biggest argument is the range of challenges he accepted during his career. He competed across multiple weight classes and continued moving up to face bigger opponents.His most notable recent challenge came against Canelo Álvarez. Crawford moved up two divisions to meet the Mexican superstar. The fight gave him another opportunity to test himself against one of boxing’s biggest names.Crawford entered that fight with an undefeated record and an undisputed championship legacy. He had already established himself as a champion in multiple divisions.His career included major wins across lightweight, light welterweight and welterweight. Crawford became undisputed at light welterweight and later achieved the same feat at welterweight.He then moved into the super middleweight division for his showdown with Canelo.That willingness to move through the divisions is central to Crawford’s argument.Khabib’s career followed a different path. The Russian retired with a perfect 29-0 MMA record. He spent most of his career competing at lightweight and became one of the most dominant champions in UFC history.Khabib defeated several elite opponents during his run. His wins included Conor McGregor, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje.However, unlike Crawford, Khabib did not move through several weight classes during his UFC career. He remained at lightweight and retired as the division’s champion.The two athletes also competed in different sports, making direct comparisons difficult.Boxing and MMA have different ranking systems, championship structures and weight divisions. Fighters also face different styles and physical demands depending on their sport.Crawford’s comments are therefore based on how he values the strength and variety of his opponents.His undefeated record remains one of the defining parts of his legacy. The Canelo fight also added another major name to a career built around championship success.Khabib, meanwhile, retired without a defeat and with a 29-0 record. His unbeaten run included a dominant UFC title reign.Both fighters finished their careers undefeated and established themselves as major figures in combat sports.
Article Summary: Terence Crawford has made a bold claim about his boxing legacy. The undefeated former champion believes his resume is far more impressive than Khabib Nurmagomedov’s MMA record. Crawford said the difference between their careers is ‘night and day’ while pointing to the quality and variety of opponents he has faced.

Article Title: Ecology to aspiration: Art reflects the many faces of paradise
Article Text:
The programme brought artists together to explore ideas of paradise and the gap between promise and reality

Attendees take a keen look at Digbijayee Khatua's artworks

Rajeev Sethi, Shivani Sibal and Teesta Bhandare

Moving away from the commerciality of art

Namita Gokhale and Rajeev Lochan

Veer Munshi

Shailesh BR is checking the working of his tech-coded installation

Kodanda Rao Teppala and Digbijayee Khatua





Characterised by a quiet, unhurried pace, the quaint village of Salogra in Himachal Pradesh’s Solan district became a temporary creative home for six artists. Over two weeks, they lived in the same space at the art residency, worked and exchanged ideas across different mediums, perspectives and practices as they explored the theme of Paradise Promised, later presented at Bikaner House.The exhibition, which concluded last month, marked the debut of art collector and advisor Teesta Bhandare’s The Knowledge Convergence Foundation (TKCF), bringing to Delhi works that emerged from its inaugural multidisciplinary and multigenerational residency programme.The programme brought together artists Rekha Hebbar Rao, Veer Munshi, Kodanda Rao Teppala, Sheena Maria Piedade, Digbijayee Khatua and Dhiraj Pednekar, along with curatorial advisor Lina Vincent. It invited the artists to look at paradise not simply as an ideal, but as a promise that shapes individual aspirations and collective realities. Given their varied practices, they responded to the theme through their own experiences, opening up questions of ecology, belonging, displacement, memory and aspiration.The residency was designed to give artists time and space to experiment, away from the usual demands of everyday life and of the commercial art ecosystem.Talking about it, Teesta told us, “It’s interesting because the concept allows us to engage directly with a lot of artists, and helps us get to know the thoughts that shape their practice. The idea behind this is to move away from the commerciality of art. The residency gave creative practitioners a chance to explore and do things that they wouldn’t ordinarily do while creating art. It was a rewarding experience.”She added, “The multigenerational format also brought artists, between the ages of 30 and 79, and at different stages of practice, into conversation.”The exhibition further expanded the conversation with works of artists Shailesh BR, Akshata Mokashi and Dhiraj Rabha, whose practices align with the curatorial theme.
Article Summary: The exhibition marked the debut of art collector Teesta Bhandare’s The Knowledge Convergence Foundation (TKCF) It brought to Delhi works that emerged from its inaugural multidisciplinary and multigenerational residency programme. The residency was designed to give artists time and space to experiment, away from the usual demands of everyday life.

Article Title: IITs bars 22 companies from placements for revoking job offers
Article Text:
Twenty-two companies that revoked job offers will not participate in upcoming placement seasons at IITs.





MUMBAI: Twenty-two companies that offered jobs to about 150 students during the 2025-26 placement season and later withdrew those offers will not be invited to participate in the next two internship and placement seasons at the IITs.The decision follows “non-cooperation” with placement teams. Among those affected were some of India’s brightest students with strong academic records, selected by companies that visited campuses in the very first week of recruitment.The decision followed an attempt to salvage the commitments. After placement teams from across the IITs met in early Sept, they approached the companies and urged them to honour their offers. Some agreed to take students at a later date in October or November and are in the process of sending written commitments. Others said they could no longer take the students on board.TOI was the first to report on June 22 that the All IITs Placement Committee (AIPC) was cracking down on recruiters revoking job offers. AIPC convenor Prof John Jose said the companies were concentrated in software, data science and edtech, with IT and software firms accounting for the largest share.“Some of these are legacy recruiters and what we call as popular companies among our students, some come to recruit as early as in the first week of placements. Their recruits included very strong candidates with good academic records,” said Prof Jose.The explanations reflected businesses under strain: financial difficulties, altered business models and projects that had disappeared, taking the anticipated need for new employees with them.“Some of them said they were in a bad shape, some said their business model had to change, and some others said many of their projects had been cancelled because of which they no longer needed more people on their rolls,” said prof Jose. Other companies contacted by the IITs did not answer calls from placement heads.For the students, the immediate task was to find another opening. Individual IIT placement committees approached other recruiters, who hired some of the affected candidates. “About 20-25% students were placed in this manner,” prof Jose said. Students also turned to their own networks, seeking referrals and exploring opportunities outside campus recruitment. “Once the students learnt about the situation, some began exploring opportunities through personal referrals, informal networks and lateral hiring. Some are actively speaking to other companies and finding jobs,” he added.For those still without work, a further question remains: whether they can return to campus for another placement season. AIPC has left that decision to individual institutes. The 2026-27 placement season begins on December 1; whether it offers another opportunity to graduates whose earlier offers fell through will depend on their respective IITs.
Article Summary: Twenty-two companies that revoked job offers will not participate in upcoming placement seasons at IITs. Among those affected were some of India's brightest students with strong academic records. The companies were concentrated in software, data science and edtech, with IT and software firms accounting for the largest share.

Article Title: A self-funded centre keeping Gandhian flame alive in Marathwada
Article Text:
Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: A building in the Silk Mill Colony of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has been quietly keeping the Gandhian thought alive for both younger and older generations.Known as the Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan, the hub serves as a critical reference point for students, activists, and researchers seeking to explore Gandhian literature, khadi spinning, and the core concept of Sarvodaya—the welfare of all.Dnyanprakash Modani, the 77-year-old Gandhian thinker, who started the full-fledged centre to coincide with the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi in 2019, said that the principles and methods of Gandhiji can still strongly appeal to modern audiences if they are presented through a contemporary lens.“With its inclusive approach, our centre brings together Gandhians under one roof, making it one of the few surviving spaces for non-violent, secular, and democratic discourse in the region,” he said.A full-panel pictorial exhibition titled ‘Mohan se Mahatma’, tracing the journey of Mohandas to the Mahatma, is one of the highlights of the centre.“The evolution of Gandhiji from a commoner into a towering personality revered as the ‘Mahatma’ itself sets off a journey of inner transformation for many.Our exhibition has captured the key moments of his life,” Modani said.The list of activities at the centre is long and diverse. It regularly conducts Sutkatai Prashikshan, which is training in spinning on the charkha—the symbol of self-reliance. It also runs classes in music, painting, sculpture, acting, and other arts. For students who have dropped out of the formal education system, the centre provides special educational support to bring them back into mainstream education. It also offers career guidance and counselling for school and college students.For those interested in deeper study, the centre conducts Grantha Shikshan, which includes study circles on the life and works of Gandhi, Phule, Ambedkar, and saint literature. To propagate the life, work, and philosophy of Gandhiji, it organises lectures, study classes, residential camps, and seminars, while also creating new literature. Its Sujana-Sajag Nagarik Abhiyan is a campaign to create aware, sensitive, and constitutionally committed citizens in the light of Gandhian thought. Besides, the bhavan is also known as the main organiser of the city-level Gandhi jayanti celebrations on Oct 2 at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in Shahganj.Notably, the establishment is entirely self-financed without a single rupee of govt grants, foreign funding, or even public donations—perhaps making it the only such institution in the country.“At a time when Gandhian institutions are struggling, it is our honest attempt to ensure the father of the nation does not remain only in history books, but becomes a living method of personal and social change,” Modani said.He added, “Great scientist Albert Einstein famously said that future generations will scarcely believe that a man like Gandhiji ever walked the earth. As one of our goals, we endeavour to raise our collective understanding of society so that people will actually understand what the words of Einstein mean.”
Article Summary: The Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is a hub for Gandhian thought. It is run by 77-year-old Dnyanprakash Modani, who started the centre to coincide with the 150th birth anniversary of Gandhi in 2019. It organises lectures, study classes, residential camps, and seminars, while also creating new literature.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: 16 years after construction, KDMC mayor finally moves into civic bungalow
Article Text:
The bungalow was constructed in 2010.





KALYAN: Sixteen years after it was constructed, the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s (KDMC) new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant, with mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performing the vastu shanti puja and entering the bungalow on Wednesday.The bungalow was constructed in 2010. However, a dispute over access to the property kept the residence largely unused for years. Several mayors subsequently attempted to resolve the road issue, but the efforts failed as villagers whose land was required for the access road were reportedly unwilling to part with the land.Even after the civic body spent lakhs of rupees on repairs, the bungalow remained unused. Former mayor Vinita Rane had performed a puja at the residence but chose not to stay there.With prolonged neglect, wooden furniture inside the bungalow was damaged and several portions were affected by termites. The civic administration later undertook extensive repairs to make the premises habitable again.After taking charge as mayor in February, Thavil took up the long-pending access issue. As she travels daily from Titwala to Kalyan, she personally held meetings with villagers and discussed their concerns. Following the resolution of the issues, the access road was finally constructed, paving the way for the mayoral residence to be used.After the road was made accessible and the neglected bungalow was completely repaired, Thavil finally entered the Adharwadi residence on Wednesday, bringing an end to the 16-year wait for the civic property to be put to its intended use.
Article Summary: Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant. Mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performed the vastu shanti puja and entered the bungalow on Wednesday.

Article Title: Kavan: What's Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar got to do with an opera?
Article Text:
A scene from the presentation

Ambedkarite by thought, not necessarily by birth

The combination of politics and art stands out for me in Kavan. And to get to work with performers from Yalgaar who are politically, theatrically and musically at the top of their game is an honour for any director Abhishek Majumdar, director

Love and friendship as binding factors

People often stay away from political or critical theatre presentations today. Our approach is that we will present our thoughts no matter what. Hopefully, it will encourage more people to think beyond their limited world view Dhammarakshit Randive, performer

BOX

What is Kavan?

As artistes, it’s equally important to watch the performances of other artistes and experiencing interdisciplinary presentations. It changes our perceptions and helps us grow. We're glad to be collaborating via Peace Projects Inter-Acts on bringing such experiences to a wider audience Parna Pethe, actor and one of the collaborators

Where

When

Timing





The moment you hear the word opera, you picture a grand musical presentation with fine costumes and trained singers performing for an audience that has paid a sizeable amount on the tickets. But Kavan turns this identity upside down. "The common perception of an opera is that it's grand and meant for the elite. We wanted to question this perception. An opera can be staged by anyone. Through Kavan, we are doing it in our style with the tools available to us," says Dhammarakshit Randive, one of the performers.An Ambedkarite opera, Kavan will make its Pune debut today. The theatrical presentation predominantly uses music – rap, folk and electronic - but is a mix of acts and audio-visuals that are connected through Sudesh Jadhav's story. "At its heart this is a story of love and friendship," says Randive, highlighting the uniting power of both in a divisive world. Kavan has its roots in the shahiri tradition of folk performances, the writings of which have long highlighted social issues.Elaborating on that, Randive says, "What Shahirs wrote was not something to just read. It was meant to be performed as well. Kavan gets its name from this tradition, and this is our way of carrying that legacy forward." Randive, who has been involved in the Ambedkarite cultural movement for over a decade, also specifies that this is an Ambedkarite opera because everyone involved identifies with the thought process. "Not everyone in our team is born a dalit," he explains, adding, "But everyone identifies with Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar's thoughts on caste bias, the Indian Constitution and more. One becomes an Ambedkarite by thought, irrespective of gender, religion or anything else. That's also the kind of diversity that we have in our collective."Through Yalgaar Sanskrutik Manch and Nalanda Arts Studio, Kavan is tapping into new audiences. While the collective has been doing folk and street performances across Maharashtra for a while, this is their first tryst with proscenium theatre. The opera had its opening show at Prithvi Theatre and travelled to Goa and Karnataka as well. "We're glad to be using this platform to take our thoughts to a newer set of people, and not limiting them to internal discussions within the collective. It's not propaganda. In fact, the core themes of love and friendship act as binding factors in a world divided in the name of religion, cast views and what not," says Randive. Abhishek Majumdar, the director of the play, adds, "As a society we don’t want to give up the privileges we have, and because of that we don't understand that what makes us strong is our ability to create equality. That is the idea of society that Babasaheb Ambedkar created the India Constitution with and it’s what we signed up for. I hope even those who disagree with the Ambedkarite view are able to have a conversation after watching Kavan.”In a rapidly changing India, young Bejul and those around him navigate their dreams, desires, dilemmas while also negotiating caste and class. An operatic satire, written and performed fully in poetry and songs about young Ambedkarite experiences, Kavan attempts to encapsulate the rapidly changing India we see around ourselves - a country with mounting ambition, full of contradictions. Where do we go when the boundaries between right and wrong, sacred and profane, personal and universal are blurred? The opera has music and songs by BamBoy and MD Pallavi. It features Siddharth Pratibhawant, Pravin Mukta, Priypal Dashantee, Dhammarakshit Randhive, Amruta Todarmal and Apurva Kadam on stage.: The Box, Erandwane;: October 2, 2026;: 4 pm and 8 pm
Article Summary: An Ambedkarite opera, Kavan will make its Pune debut today. The theatrical presentation predominantly uses music – rap, folk and electronic - but is a mix of acts and audio-visuals. Kavan has its roots in the shahiri tradition of folk performances, the writings of which have long highlighted social issues.
